1. For some reason, I mix up vinegar and vagina.

Me: Do you like... vinegar?

Colleague: Sure.

Me: Actually, I hesitated a bit before saying that, because I always mix up those two words...

Colleague: Hahaha, I like both. How else would I have three kids?

Me: .......

2. Another time I went to a Dutch supermarket to buy adhesive hooks. I couldn’t find them, so I asked a shop assistant and, God knows why, asked whether they had any sticky hookers. He thought for a moment, more or less worked out what I meant, and took me to find them. After a while he just couldn’t hold it in: are you sure that’s what they’re called?!

3. And one in German, when I hadn’t been learning it for long.

Some people who build rail vehicles (Schienenfahrzeuge) came to the institute, and I sat in on their meeting with my boss. Afterward a German colleague asked me what the visitors worked on. I said Schinken. He looked utterly baffled... Then I said it again in English, and he cracked up on the spot.

Schinken = ham

Couldn’t someone at least have come to talk about a project on postpartum care for sows?

Curious about the years a guy from Northeast China has spent knocking around European academia and industry? See my Zhihu column PhD Diaries.
